Mahalaleel
mä-hal'a-lē-el
n. (the son of Cainan and fifth in the line from Adam, whose name means the praise of God; called Maleleel by Luke)
From Hebrew Mahalal'el, from mahalal, praise, and El, God — praise of God, or he that praises God. Luke's Greek gives Maleleel. A later Mahalaleel of the tribe of Judah is named among the dwellers in Jerusalem after the captivity (Neh 11:4).

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Mahalaleel is the fifth link in the chain from Adam to Noah, and the record of him is three verses long: “And Cainan lived seventy years, and begat Mahalaleel” (Gen 5:12); “And Mahalaleel lived sixty and five years, and begat Jared” (Gen 5:15); “And all the days of Mahalaleel were eight hundred ninety and five years: and he died” (Gen 5:17). Luke names him in the ascent to Adam as Maleleel (Luk 3:37). What the entry is worth attending to is the name, because the names of Genesis 5 read as a confession when they are laid end to end. Seth, appointed; Enos, frail man; Cainan, possession; Mahalaleel, the praise of God; Jared, descent; Enoch, dedicated; Methuselah; Lamech; Noah, rest. In the very generations under the sentence of death, a father named his son the praise of God. Nothing whatever is recorded of the man's deeds. What is recorded is what a family in the line of promise called their children while the world of Cain was building cities and singing Lamech's song of vengeance.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) has no article for Mahalaleel; in sacred history he is the son of Cainan, fifth from Adam, called Maleleel in the Gospel of Luke.

MAHALALEEL, n. The praise of God; the son of Cainan and the father of Jared.

He is the fifth in descent from Adam in the line of Seth.

He lived sixty and five years and begat Jared.

All the days of Mahalaleel were eight hundred ninety and five years, and he died.

In Luke's genealogy the Greek form Maleleel is used.

Gen 5:12 — "And Cainan lived seventy years, and begat Mahalaleel:"

Gen 5:15 — "And Mahalaleel lived sixty and five years, and begat Jared:"

Gen 5:17 — "And all the days of Mahalaleel were eight hundred ninety and five years: and he died."

Luk 3:37 — "Which was the son of Mathusala, which was the son of Enoch, which was the son of Jared, which was the son of Maleleel, which was the son of Cainan,"

Modern Corruption

There is no significant modern redefinition of this name. The principle to recover is that naming is confession, and that parents in the covenant line have always spoken their theology over their children before those children could speak at all.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. Mahalaleel is a patriarch in a register and nobody has contested him. What his name sets against the modern practice is the seriousness with which Scripture treats naming. In the line of Seth the names carry God in them — Mahalal-el, praise of God — while in the parallel line of Cain the names carry the man: a city named after a son, a boast named after a father. Genesis puts the two registers side by side in chapters 4 and 5 and lets the reader hear the difference in what each family thought worth saying.

The principle to recover is that a household's speech forms its children long before its arguments do. The covenant instruction of Deuteronomy assumes exactly this: the words are to be in the heart, taught diligently, talked of when thou sittest in thine house and when thou walkest by the way (Deu 6:6-7). Paul commands fathers to bring them up “in the nurture and admonition of the Lord” (Eph 6:4). A man who called his son the praise of God in the eight hundredth year of a dying world was doing what Christian fathers still do at a font and a supper table: saying out loud, over a child who cannot yet answer, whose the house is.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Mahalal'el (H4111), praise of God; mahalal (H4110), praise; El (H410), God; halal (H1984), to praise, to shine; Greek Maleleel (G3121).

Hebrew Mahalal'el (H4111) — Mahalaleel; the praise of God.

Hebrew mahalal (H4110) — praise; the first element of the name.

Hebrew El (H410) — God; the second element.

Hebrew halal (H1984) — to praise; the root that gives Hallelujah.

Greek Maleleel (G3121) — the form in Luke's genealogy.

Usage

"“And Cainan lived seventy years, and begat Mahalaleel” — the line kept and dated."

"“The praise of God” — a confession spoken over a child in a dying world."

"“Which was the son of Maleleel” — the name carried into the Gospel."
